the stripe phase is characterized by spatial modulations of the Cu 2d and O 3p energies, and that these energy modulations are consistent with a valence-bomb-solid interpretation of the charge order.
the Cu 3$d$ and O 2$p$ energies are modulated in the stripe phase and the energy shifts can be interpreted in a valence bond solid framework.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the charge and spin dynamics in cuprate superconducting materials.
the electronic structure of high temperature superconductors and the nature of charge order in these materials.
the electronic structure of high-Tc cuprate superconducting materials, and how this structure changes with the application of magnetic fields and the introduction of defects.

stripe order in LNSCO is a spatial modulation of electronic energies.
the stripe phase in the cuprates is a spatially modulated electronic structure.
stripes in the cuprate high temperature superconductors are a spatial modulation in both the charge and energy densities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stripe ordering in LNSCO leads to spatially inhomogeneous electronic structure, which can be described in terms of spatially modulated Cu 3d valence and O 2$p$ hole densities.
the stripes are not simply charge density modulations.
the stripes are not a simple charge density wave, but a complex modulation in electronic structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the charge order in LNSCO is a subtle phenomenon and the common picture of charge order is not a complete description.
stripe order in cuprates is not a simple modulation of the charge distribution, but rather a more complex modulation of the local electronic structure.
the charge modulation is not the dominant signature of stripe order, which is instead a modulation in the electronic structure of Cu and O atoms in the plane.
